newsitem.title: USA: Consolidated Paper buying rival in $674 million deal.
newsitem.headline: Consolidated Paper buying rival in $674 million deal.

text.p: Consolidated Papers Inc. said Wednesday it agreed to buy the Wisconsin paper operations of a troubled Canadian paper maker in a $674 million deal that will strengthen its position as the biggest U.S. producer of coated printing paper.
Consolidated Papers will pay $227 million in cash and assume $447 million in debt to buy Repap Wisconsin Inc., a Kimberly, Wis., maker of coated papers, from Repap Enterprises Inc.

Repap Enterprises is a Montreal-based paper maker that has suffered in recent years from heavy debts and weak demand for coated paper. Repap's British Columbia pulp-making unit in March sought protection from creditors.

Repap Wisconsin, with capacity to make 508,000 tons of coated paper a year, had 1996 sales of $405 million and about 1,000 employees. Its papers are used in brochures, advertising inserts, annual reports, catalogues and magazines.

Consolidated Papers, with annual capacity of 1.3 million tons of coated paper, earned $179 million, or $4.01 a share, on sales of $1.5 billion last year. The company, which has 6,000 workers, is based in Wisconsin Rapids, about 100 miles from the operations of Repap Wisconsin.
Repap Wisconsin's sales and marketing affiliate, as well as a groundwood pulp mill and a paper recycling facility, will be included in the transaction.

Analyst Brian Topp of BZW Canada said Repap got a good price for its operations in Wisconsin. "I was pleasantly surprised by how much money they got. It was certainly in excess of what I thought they would receive," Topp said.
Repap said it also agreed to sell other paper and lumber operations in The Pas, Manitoba, to Tolko Industries Ltd., a closely held company based in British Columbia. Terms were not disclosed.
The tentative agreement with Consolidated Papers is subject to approval of both companies' boards of directors and federal regulators and the final price may be adjusted, Consolidated said.

"This acquisition expands our presence in the coated paper marketplace (and) positions us to better serve existing and new customers," Consolidated President Gorton Evans said in a statement. "The products they produce are consistent with the type and quality of the coated papers we already make."
Consolidated Papers also makes paperboard, paperboard products, corrugated displays and containers. Its stock fell 75 cents to $55.875 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly after midday.

Repap Enterprises stock rose 10 cents Canadian (7 cents U.S.) to 48 cents (35 cents U.S.) on the Toronto Stock Exchange. The sale to Consolidated is expected to close in the third quarter, Consolidated said.
